subject: Installation of Poet Laureate Max Heinegg
overview: The City of Medford hosted a ceremony to officially install Max Heinegg as its third Poet Laureate and to honor the contributions of outgoing Poet Laureate Vijaya Sundaram.

items.title: Introductory Remarks
items.summary: Mayor Breanna Lungo-Koehn welcomed attendees, introduced the Poet Laureate Program, and thanked outgoing Poet Laureate Vijaya Sundaram.

items.title: Poetry Reading by Terry Carter
items.summary: Medford's inaugural Poet Laureate Terry Carter performed his poem, "When the Lions Don't Roar."

items.title: Remarks from the Medford Arts Council
items.summary: Medford Arts Council Co-Chair Leticia Rocha shared the goals of the council, announced the upcoming grant cycle, and praised the work of both the outgoing and incoming poet laureates.

items.title: Poetry Reading by Vijaya Sundaram
items.summary: Outgoing Poet Laureate Vijaya Sundaram read her poem, "All Our Yesterdays," and spoke on the connection between teaching, poetry, and community.

items.title: Installation and Reading by Max Heinegg
items.summary: Mayor Breanna Lungo-Koehn officially installed Max Heinegg as the new Poet Laureate, who then read a commemorative poem reflecting on his history as an educator and resident in Medford.
